title: Degradation → QBR: RCA & Escalation Matrix (Operational Playbook)
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview:
This playbook defines the operational path from an observed service degradation to coordinated RCA (root cause analysis) and structured QBR (quarterly business review) follow-up with enterprise customers. It standardizes detection signals, triage windows, escalation matrix, customer communication templates, and handoff into QBR action items. The goal is to reduce time-to-resolution, maintain consistent customer comms, and ensure learnings feed back into product/infra roadmaps.

Scope:
- Applies to enterprise customers on Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Covers degradations that affect availability, response latency (generation or embedding), cost-per-token anomalies, or model-quality regressions tied to a deployed model version.
- Excludes planned maintenance (use go-live/maintenance communications).

Key definitions:
- Degradation: measurable negative change in service behavior relative to SLOs (availability, latency, quality, cost).
- Severity Levels: S1 (critical outage affecting >10% of requests or single-customer availability loss), S2 (degraded latency or increased error rates for targeted routes/customers), S3 (minor quality deviations or cost anomalies for small cohort).
- Triage Window: time budget to perform initial diagnosis before customer communication; varies by severity (see Matrix).

Escalation & Triage Matrix (quick reference):
| Signal | Detection Query (examples) | Threshold | Initial Owner | Triage Window | Escalation Action |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| API 5xx spike (multi-customer) | rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.*"}[5m]) > 0.02 | >2% 5xx rate over 5m | Platform SRE | 15m | Open incident, notify CS Ops, page infra on-call |
| Per-customer availability drop | sum(rate(requests_failed{customer_id="$CID"}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{customer_id="$CID"}[5m])) > 0.05 | >5% | Customer Success (CS) + Tenant Ops | 30m | Initiate customer-specific status, add to incident if cross-tenant |
| Latency p95 increase (generation) | histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le)(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[10m]))) | p95 > 350ms | Serving Runtime Team | 30m | Run perf profile, check KV-cache hitrate, notify CS |
| Model quality regression (eval failures) | failed_prompts_total{model=~"v.*"}[1h] > baseline + 20% | +20% vs baseline evaluation set | Applied ML | 1h | Revert model variant or enable fallback, inform CS + Product |
| Cost-per-token anomaly | cost_per_token_daily{customer_id="$CID"} > expected * 3 | >3x | Billing / Cost Ops | 24h | Block suspicious routes, notify account owner |

Note: The Prometheus/Query examples are implementation patterns. Teams must keep authoritative queries in the shared dashboard library (see Related pages).

Detailed Playbook: Detection → RCA → QBR Handoff
1) Detection (0–15 minutes for S1, 0–30 minutes S2):
  - Automated alert fires into PagerDuty / Opsgenie and creates an incident in Incident Manager.
  - CS Ops watches customer-specific alerts via the Customer Health Sentinel and flag impacted accounts.
  - First responder confirms whether degradation is internal, external (cloud provider), or customer-side (network/VPC misconfig).

2) Initial Triage (15–60 minutes depending on severity):
  - Gather: recent deploys/rollouts, model versions, routing fallback events, kernel/quantization changes, config changes.
  - Key telemetry to collect: per-tenant request rates, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx/error class breakdown, KV cache hit rate, model variant IDs, GPU-queue lengths, and cost burn rate.
  - Use these canonical queries (examples):
    - Per-customer 5xx rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.*",customer_id="$CID"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{customer_id="$CID"}[5m]))
    - KV cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookup_total[5m]))
    - Model variant rollouts: SELECT deploy_id, model_version, started_at FROM model_rollouts WHERE started_at > now() - interval '90 minutes';

3) Communication (within triage window):
  - If S1/S2: CS Ops posts an initial templated update to the customer within 60 minutes (see templates below) and provides hourly updates until mitigated.
  - If S3: CS Ops prepares a targeted message for affected customers and aims for communication within 24 hours.
  - All outbound communications must include: what we know, what we're doing, ETA for next update, and contact for escalation.

4) Mitigation & Short-term Fix (1–6 hours):
  - Mitigation options: route to fallback model variant, increase pod count in Dedicated pool, enable prefix-KV cache warming, fail open to cheaper model for non-critical routes, or rollback last deploy.
  - Ownership: infra/runtime teams execute mitigation; CS tracks customer-facing changes and confirms impact.

5) Root Cause Analysis (24–72 hours):
  - Post-incident, the owning engineering team produces an RCA document with: timeline, contributing factors, corrective actions, risk assessment, and detection gaps.
  - CS consolidates customer impact summary (who, when, duration, measurable customer effects) into a one-page incident summary.

6) QBR Handoff & Action Itemization (1–2 weeks):
  - Any customer impacted by an S1 or repeated S2 for >2 incidents in a quarter is flagged for QBR agenda.
  - Handoff packet to QBR owner (CS lead) must include: incident summary, RCA link, proposed triage & product mitigations, ETA for fixes, and customer-facing remediation (credits, SLAs).
  - The QBR agenda item template: context → timeline → business impact metrics → remediation plan → prevention roadmap → open decisions.

Ownership Matrix (who does what):
- CS Ops: customer notifications, ticket routing, QBR agenda coordination, executive summaries.
- Platform SRE: multi-tenant infra issues, cloud provider escalations, incident commander for S1s.
- Serving Runtime: profiling, kernel/quantization rollback, scaling actions.
- Applied ML: model evaluation, rollback of model variants, quality investigation.
- Billing/Cost Ops: cost anomalies, credits, billing adjustments.

Customer Communication Templates (examples)
- Initial S1 update (subject): "[Redwood] Incident: Service degradation affecting requests — investigating"
  Body (first update):
  "We’re investigating increased error rates impacting API requests. What we know: Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat; Scope: ~12% of production traffic; Started: 2026-02-15 09:12 UTC. What we’re doing: paging infra and runtime teams, running targeted rollbacks for the most recent model rollout, and applying read-through cache warming. Next update: in 60 minutes. Contact: cs-ops@redwood.ai"

- RCA summary template (one page):
  - Incident ID, Start/End, Customers impacted (list), Root cause (summary), Contributing factors (bullet list), Actions taken, Long-term mitigations, Estimated customer impact (hours, failed requests, revenue exposure).

Acceptance & Escalation Criteria (examples)
- Move incident to QBR: any single customer experiencing >2 hours of degraded availability in a 30-day window, or any S1 affecting enterprise revenue.
- Automatic escalation to senior leadership: when an incident triggers cross-region failover or when SLA credits > $50k are projected.

Postmortem and QBR Integration:
- For flagged incidents, CS includes incident summaries in the next QBR as a discrete item with a clear set of owner-assigned actions and timelines. The QBR should always close actions or re-prioritize into the product roadmap with a named owner and ETA.
- Template QBR action tracking columns: Action, Owner, Due Date, Status, Customer Impact Metric, Link to PR/Issue.

Operational tooling & dashboards to maintain:
- Customer Health Sentinel: per-tenant SLO heatmap and active incident list.
- Degradation Triager dashboard: top N errors by route, per-model quality drift graphs, KV cache hit rate, GPU queue depth.
- Cost anomaly tracker: rolling 24h cost-per-token by customer and model variant.

Runbook snippets (one-line commands):
- Re-route traffic to fallback variant (CLI): redwoodctl traffic reroute --from model:v2.3 --to model:v2.2 --percent 100 --tenant $CID
- Inspect model rollout history (SQL): SELECT * FROM model_rollouts WHERE model_version = 'v2.3' ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 20;

Governance & SLOs referenced:
- Platform availability SLO: 99.95% global per month (excl. maintenance windows).
- p95 latency target (generation): 350ms for hosted API default route; per-customer contracts may differ.
- Quality SLOs: baseline eval pass-rate > 92% for curated prompt-sets.

Appendix: Example queries and alerts to copy into the shared alerts library:
- Alert: CUSTOMER_AVAILABILITY_DROP
  Query: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{customer_id="$CID",status=~"5.*"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{customer_id="$CID"}[5m]))) > 0.05
  Severity: S2
  Notify: cs-ops, tenant-ops, serving-runtime

- Alert: MODEL_QUALITY_REGRESSION
  Query: increase(failed_prompts_total{model=~"production-.*"}[1h]) > 0.2 * baseline_failed_prompts
  Severity: S2
  Notify: applied-ml, cs-ops
